messages:
pagerduty: INCIDENT: [P0] gpu-host-210b kernel panic -> kubelet NotReady -> page fired for rotation. Host: gpu-host-210b (us-west-2a). Alert: host unreachable + kernel oops on nvme driver. Pager: pagerduty

sre-bot: automated page: severity=P0, runbook=/runbooks/gpu-host-kernel-panic.md, suggested-actions=CORDON->DRAIN->INVESTIGATE, pagerduty_id=PD-87432

Maya (oncall): ack'd. I'm on it. Starting triage. First: confirm host status and whether pods are evicted or still running. @statusbot can you cut a preliminary incident note? :eyes:

statusbot: status page draft created: https://status.redwood-inference.example/incidents/PD-87432 (private). Marking "investigating".

Maya (oncall): kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-host-210b

```
NAME             STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-host-210b    NotReady   <none>   72d   v1.27.3
```

Maya (oncall): kubectl describe node gpu-host-210b -> shows "kernel: panic - stack trace" and kubelet marking node notready. dmesg on host not accessible via regular ssh (host unreachable).

Raj: are control-plane components healthy? Any API server errors? I can check kubelet logs from kube-proxy/node-exporter.

Liam (next-oncall): I'm standing by for handoff if you need. If it's a kernel oops we likely need infra to repro or attach serial console. Cordon and drain if pods will impact customer traffic.

Maya (oncall): cordon first to stop new pods

```
kubectl cordon gpu-host-210b
node/gpu-host-210b cordoned
```

Maya (oncall): begin draining non-daemonset pods with grace 120s and ignore-daemonsets

```
kubectl drain gpu-host-210b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```

Alex: heads-up - there are stateful pods pinned to this node for some customers (batching workers). We'll force evict where possible but open a migration ticket. I'll notify impacted teams: @ml-platform.

Olivia: checking scheduler logs - we saw a small spike in IO errors from NVMe on that node 2m before the panic. Might be NVMe firmware + driver race.

Maya (oncall): capturing current workloads that will be rescheduled

```
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-host-210b
NAMESPACE     NAME                             READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE    IP
ml-prod       batch-worker-87                   1/1     Running   0          3d    10.10.7.23
inference     gpu-infer-3                       1/1     Running   0          6h    10.10.7.45
```

Maya (oncall): eviction started. Most pods rescheduled to other GPUs. Observability: traffic drop at region level? @statusbot update if customer-facing endpoints impacted.

statusbot: No publicly visible endpoint degradation detected. Internal metric: 5% increase in inference latency for region us-west-2 for 2 minutes; flagging.

Raj: can someone grab the serial console logs from the host via infra? I'll ask infra. @infra please attach console output and check kernel oops / backtrace.

Maya (oncall): paging infra on-call now. PD escalation level -> infra oncall.

pagerduty: PD escalation: infra-oncall paged (infra-oliver). Acknowledgement pending.

Oliver (infra-oncall): ack. Pulling serial console. Preliminary: "Kernel panic - stack trace: nvme_core + 0x..." Looks like nvme driver trapped. Also see repeated I/O timeouts before panic.

Maya (oncall): good info. Action plan so far: 1) cordon + drain (done) 2) evacuate workloads 3) if node doesn't come back, decommission and reprovision host 4) collect dmesg / serial logs and attach to PD ticket 5) notify affected customers if SLA risk.

Alex: creating infra ticket to reprovision host and attach logs -> TKT-3429. Adding owners: @infra, @ml-platform.

Liam (next-oncall): handing off monitoring and any remaining customer comms. Maya, do you want me to stay on infra call while you finish triage? I can take postmortem owner if you want.

Maya (oncall): thanks. Yes please take postmortem. I'll stay to confirm node state & confirm that replacement host is up and workloads are stable. @olivia please run health checks on affected workloads.

Olivia: running perf and correctness checks on inference jobs. Quick smoke test: 10 queries to gpu-infer nodes - passing, latency within normal range for new hosts.

Maya (oncall): infra reports host failed full hardware health check and is marked for reprovision. ETA for new host in same AZ: ~14 minutes. Moving to degraded -> partial capacity. Notifying customers on private incidents if they had pinned resources.

Alex: pinged ML-platform and CS for any customers with reserved capacity on that node. Preparing templated message.

Maya (oncall): updating incident note with timeline and mitigations. We'll keep page open until replacement up and all pods stable. Current impact: transient latency spike, a small number of batch jobs restarted. No data loss detected. Severity remains P1 -> reviewing for P0 downgrade after stable.

statusbot: incident timeline updated. Next update scheduled in 10 minutes or on state change.

Oliver (infra-oncall): reprovision job started. Will attach firmware revision and nvme SMART output when ready. Suspect firmware mismatch; capturing HW serials.

Liam (next-oncall): taking over rotation in 5 minutes. Maya — handoff: node cordoned/draining, infra reprovisioning, customers notified if reserved. Postmortem owner: Liam. Anything else I should call out?

Maya (oncall): handoff ack. Please capture the following in postmortem: kernel oops backtrace, nvme SMART logs, firmware levels, kubelet events around eviction, and whether autoscaler could be tuned to avoid customer pain during single-node failures. I'll forward any extra logs I collect.

Liam (next-oncall): ack — I'll own postmortem, link PD ticket, and schedule 1-hour blameless postmortem tomorrow. Closing active page once reprovisioned and cluster metrics normalize. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by Maya (oncall), Oliver (infra-oncall), Liam (next-oncall). PD-87432 owners set: Maya, Oliver, Liam.

statusbot: incident state: investigating -> mitigated (partial). Final update pending reprovision confirmation."
